title: First Cut
summary: Import footage, trim it, and export your first finished clip.
description: Every editor starts by moving one clip from a camera card to a finished file. Import any three clips you already have, cut the dead air off the front and back of each, lay them end to end, and export a single video you could actually send to someone. The goal is the round trip, not beauty.
deliverables: An exported video file of at least 20 seconds built from three trimmed clips.
victoryConditions: You imported at least three clips into a single timeline.
You trimmed the dead air from the start and end of every clip.
You exported a playable file and watched it back start to finish.
stretchGoals: Export a second version at a different resolution and compare the file sizes.
reflectionPrompt: Which step of the import-to-export round trip felt slowest, and what would you automate next time?

title: Blender Toybox
summary: Learn to orbit, pan, zoom, and place objects without fighting the viewport.
description: Blender punishes people who never learned to navigate. Open a new scene and build a small still life out of primitives: a table, a cup, a lamp. You are not modelling yet. You are proving you can move the camera and place objects on purpose instead of by accident.
deliverables: A screenshot of a still life scene built from at least four primitive objects.
victoryConditions: You orbited, panned, and zoomed the viewport using shortcuts rather than menus.
You placed at least four primitives at deliberate positions in the scene.
You saved the .blend file with a name you will recognise later.
stretchGoals: Add a second camera and switch between the two views.
reflectionPrompt: Which viewport shortcut did you reach for most, and which one do you still forget?

title: Movement Lab
summary: Set your first keyframes and watch an object move on a timeline.
description: Animation is just values changing over time. Take one object from your toybox scene and make it move: set a keyframe at the start, move to a later frame, change the position, set another keyframe. Play it back. Then do the same for rotation and scale.
deliverables: A short playblast or screen recording of one object moving, rotating, and scaling.
victoryConditions: You set keyframes on position, rotation, and scale for at least one object.
You scrubbed the timeline and saw the values interpolate between your keys.
You rendered or recorded a playback of the motion.
stretchGoals: Make the object stop and start rather than gliding at a constant speed.
reflectionPrompt: Did the motion feel mechanical or natural, and what do you think caused that?

title: Ten-Second Cinematic
summary: Plan, shoot or gather, and cut a deliberate ten-second sequence.
description: Ten seconds is long enough to need a plan and short enough to finish. Decide what the viewer should understand by the end, gather or shoot three to six shots that deliver it, and cut them so the sequence reads without narration.
deliverables: A ten-second exported sequence and the one sentence describing what it communicates.
victoryConditions: You wrote down the single idea the sequence should communicate before cutting.
You used between three and six shots in the finished sequence.
A viewer could describe what happened without you explaining it.
stretchGoals: Cut a second version that tells the same story in five seconds.
reflectionPrompt: Which shot carried the most meaning, and which one could you have dropped?

title: Pacing Duel
summary: Cut the same footage twice at different rhythms and compare the feel.
description: Pacing is a choice, not an accident. Take one set of clips and cut it twice: once slow and observational, once fast and urgent. Same material, opposite feeling. Watch both back to back and name what actually changed.
deliverables: Two exported edits of the same footage with clearly different pacing.
victoryConditions: You produced two distinct edits from one identical set of source clips.
The average shot length differs by at least a factor of two between them.
You wrote down which version suits the material better and why.
stretchGoals: Cut a third version that changes pace partway through.
reflectionPrompt: Which version did you prefer, and was that about the footage or about your habit?

title: Soundscape
summary: Build a scene's audio bed from ambience, spot effects, and levels.
description: Picture without sound is half a scene. Take one of your existing edits and build its audio: a continuous ambience underneath, two or three spot effects placed against the picture, and levels balanced so nothing fights. Mute the video and check the audio still tells you where you are.
deliverables: An edit with at least three audio layers and a balanced mix.
victoryConditions: You laid a continuous ambience track under the whole scene.
You placed at least two spot effects in sync with something on screen.
You balanced levels so no single element clips or drowns the others.
stretchGoals: Add a music bed and duck it under any dialogue or key effect.
reflectionPrompt: With the picture muted, what did the audio alone tell you about the place?

title: Color Alchemist
summary: Balance shots to match, then apply one deliberate look.
description: Colour work is two jobs in order: make the shots match, then decide how they should feel. Correct every shot in a sequence so they look like the same day and the same camera, and only then apply a single look across all of them.
deliverables: A graded sequence plus before and after stills of the same frame.
victoryConditions: You balanced every shot in the sequence so they match each other.
You applied one consistent look across the whole sequence after balancing.
You exported before and after stills of the same frame for comparison.
stretchGoals: Grade a second, opposite look and decide which serves the story.
reflectionPrompt: Did you fix the match first, or did you reach for the look too early?

title: Camera Academy
summary: Use shot size, lens choice, and movement as deliberate decisions.
description: Stop framing by default. Shoot or render the same subject as a wide, a medium, and a close-up; then repeat with a different focal length; then add one motivated camera move. The point is to feel how each choice changes what the viewer thinks the shot is about.
deliverables: A contact sheet or sequence showing three shot sizes, two focal lengths, and one camera move.
victoryConditions: You captured the same subject at three distinct shot sizes.
You compared at least two focal lengths on the same subject.
You executed one camera move that is motivated by the action, not decoration.
stretchGoals: Reshoot the weakest of the three sizes now that you know what it is for.
reflectionPrompt: Which framing changed the meaning most, and was that the one you expected?

title: The Strange Room
summary: A portfolio test: build one complete, strange, believable room sequence.
description: This is an assessment, not a lesson. Produce a short sequence set in a single room that feels deliberately off. You own every stage: the idea, the shots, the cut, the sound, and the grade. Then score yourself honestly across the six craft categories. The scores are a coaching aid, not a certificate.
deliverables: A finished sequence of 30 to 90 seconds set in one room, with sound and grade.
victoryConditions: The sequence is set in a single room and runs between 30 and 90 seconds.
You handled shooting or rendering, editing, sound, and grading yourself.
You scored all six craft categories honestly from zero to ten.
stretchGoals: Show it to one person cold and note the first thing they ask about.
reflectionPrompt: Which craft category scored lowest, and what is the smallest practice that would raise it?

title: The Mechanist
summary: Model and rig a mechanical object that moves convincingly.
description: Mechanical animation is forgiving of artistry and unforgiving of logic. Model something with moving parts, a piston, a hinge, a crank, and make it move the way physics says it must. If a part passes through another, the illusion dies.
deliverables: A rendered loop of a mechanism with at least two interlocking moving parts.
victoryConditions: The mechanism has at least two parts that move in relation to each other.
No part intersects another at any frame of the animation.
You rendered a loop that plays without a visible jump at the seam.
stretchGoals: Add a second mechanism driven by the first.
reflectionPrompt: Where did the motion break the illusion first, and how did you find it?

title: Material Library
summary: Build a reusable set of materials that read correctly under light.
description: A material that looks right in one lighting setup and wrong in another is not finished. Build five materials, metal, wood, plastic, fabric, glass, and test all five under three different lighting conditions. Keep the ones that survive.
deliverables: A render sheet showing five materials under three lighting setups.
victoryConditions: You authored five distinct materials covering different surface families.
You tested every material under at least three lighting conditions.
You saved the materials so they can be reused in another scene.
stretchGoals: Rebuild the weakest material from scratch using reference photos.
reflectionPrompt: Which material fell apart under a new light, and what was wrong in its setup?

title: World Builder
summary: Compose a full environment with depth, scale, and motivated light.
description: An environment is a composition problem, not a modelling problem. Build a scene with a clear foreground, midground, and background, light it from a source the viewer can believe in, and use atmosphere to sell the distance between layers.
deliverables: A rendered environment still with readable foreground, midground, and background.
victoryConditions: The frame has distinguishable foreground, midground, and background layers.
Every light in the scene has a visible or implied source in the world.
You used atmosphere or depth cues to separate the layers.
stretchGoals: Render the same environment at a different time of day.
reflectionPrompt: Does the scene read at a glance, or does the eye get lost hunting for the subject?

title: Puppeteer
summary: Animate a character action with believable timing and weight.
description: Characters betray bad timing instantly. Take a rigged character and animate one complete action, a lift, a jump, a turn, and make the audience believe the thing has mass. Use the Graph Editor to fix the spacing rather than adding more keys.
deliverables: A rendered character action of three to six seconds showing clear weight.
victoryConditions: The character completes one full action with a beginning, middle, and end.
You adjusted spacing in the Graph Editor rather than only adding keyframes.
The action reads as having weight when played at full speed.
stretchGoals: Animate the same action again as if the object were half the weight.
reflectionPrompt: Where did you feel the weight break, and was it timing or spacing?

title: Power Core
summary: Integrate an effect into a plate so it belongs in the shot.
description: Effects fail at the seams. Add a glowing element, particles, or volumetrics to an existing shot and make it sit in the frame: matching light direction, matching grain, matching black levels. If you can point at the join, keep working.
deliverables: A composited shot with an added effect plus the clean plate for comparison.
victoryConditions: The added element matches the light direction and colour of the plate.
You matched grain and black levels between the element and the plate.
You kept the clean plate so the composite can be compared against it.
stretchGoals: Show both versions to someone and ask which frame the effect is in.
reflectionPrompt: Which mismatch gave the composite away first when you looked at it cold?

title: Raid I — The Machine
summary: A long-form build: one machine, modelled, rigged, animated, lit, and composited.
description: This is the first full pipeline run. One mechanical subject travels the whole route from blank file to finished shot: model, materials, rig, animation, lighting, render, composite, and grade. Nothing is allowed to stay a placeholder.
deliverables: A finished shot of 10 to 20 seconds taking one machine through the whole pipeline.
victoryConditions: The subject was modelled, materialled, rigged, and animated by you.
The shot was lit, rendered, composited, and graded to a finished state.
No stage of the pipeline was left as a placeholder or a default setting.
stretchGoals: Write down how long each pipeline stage actually took you.
reflectionPrompt: Which pipeline stage ate the most time, and was that the stage that mattered most?

title: One-Minute Story
summary: Tell a complete story with a beginning, a turn, and an ending in sixty seconds.
description: A minute is enough for a whole story if nothing is wasted. Write a premise in one sentence, plan the shots, and cut a sixty-second piece with a clear beginning, a turn, and an ending. No narration allowed to do the work for you.
deliverables: A sixty-second exported film plus the one-sentence premise it came from.
victoryConditions: You wrote the premise in a single sentence before shooting anything.
The finished piece has a clear beginning, a turn, and an ending.
The story reads without narration explaining what is happening.
stretchGoals: Recut it to forty seconds without losing the turn.
reflectionPrompt: Did the turn land where you planned it, or did the edit move it?

title: Raid II — Director's Cut
summary: Revise a finished piece based on real feedback until it is measurably better.
description: Making something is half the craft; revising it is the other half. Take a finished piece, show it to at least two people, collect what actually confused them, and cut a revised version that fixes the confusion rather than defending the original.
deliverables: A revised cut, the feedback notes, and a list of the changes you made.
victoryConditions: You collected feedback from at least two people who had not seen it before.
You wrote down the specific confusion each person reported.
The revised cut addresses at least three of the reported problems.
stretchGoals: Show the revision to one of the original viewers and note what changed for them.
reflectionPrompt: Which piece of feedback did you resist most, and was it right?

title: One-Person Studio
summary: Run a full production alone, on a schedule you set and keep.
description: The last skill is logistics. Plan a production with real milestones and dates, then execute it alone: concept, brief, shot list, assets, animation or shooting, render, edit, sound, colour, review, and final export. Track where the schedule slipped.
deliverables: A completed production plus the schedule showing planned versus actual dates.
victoryConditions: You wrote a schedule with dated milestones before starting production.
You carried the production through every stage to a final export.
You recorded the actual dates so planned and real can be compared.
stretchGoals: Estimate the next project using what this schedule actually taught you.
reflectionPrompt: Which stage did you underestimate most, and by how much?

title: Cinematic Master
summary: Assemble a portfolio piece that proves you can produce and revise independently.
description: The campaign ends where it was always going: one piece you would actually show someone to get work. It must be produced by you, revised at least once on real feedback, and packaged so a stranger can watch it without instructions.
deliverables: A packaged portfolio piece with a title, a description, and a shareable export.
victoryConditions: The piece was produced end to end by you without an unfinished stage.
You revised it at least once after showing it to someone else.
It is packaged so a stranger can watch it without any explanation from you.
stretchGoals: Write the two-sentence pitch you would send with it.
reflectionPrompt: If you made this again from scratch, what would you do differently first?

title: The Rough Cut Trial
summary: A first assessment: cut one short scene from footage you did not shoot for it.
description: This is an assessment, not a lesson. Take any three clips you already have and cut them into a scene that reads as intentional. No titles, no music crutch. Then score yourself honestly across the six craft categories — the scores point at your weakest area, they do not grade you.
deliverables: A cut of 15 to 40 seconds built from clips that were not shot for this scene.
victoryConditions: The cut runs between 15 and 40 seconds with no titles and no music.
Every cut point was chosen for a reason you can say out loud.
You scored all six craft categories honestly from zero to ten.
stretchGoals: Recut the same clips in a second, deliberately different order and compare.
reflectionPrompt: Which cut point was the hardest to justify, and what would make it obvious next time?

title: The Ten-Second Verdict
summary: An assessment of pacing, sound and colour working together in ten seconds.
description: This is an assessment, not a lesson. Deliver exactly ten seconds that survive being watched twice: deliberate pacing, a sound bed that carries weight, and a grade that is a choice rather than a default. Then score all six craft categories honestly.
deliverables: A ten-second piece with finished sound and a deliberate grade.
victoryConditions: The piece is ten seconds long, give or take half a second.
Sound and image were both mixed and graded on purpose, not left at defaults.
You scored all six craft categories honestly from zero to ten.
stretchGoals: Mute it and check whether the pacing still reads.
reflectionPrompt: Did the sound or the grade carry more of the weight, and why do you think that is?

title: The Machine Room
summary: An assessment of a full 3D shot: model, shade, light, render and integrate.
description: This is an assessment, not a lesson. Produce one finished shot containing a mechanical object you built, shaded, lit and rendered yourself, then integrated into a real or synthetic plate so the seam does not show. Then score all six craft categories honestly.
deliverables: A finished render of 5 to 15 seconds with the mechanical object integrated into a plate.
victoryConditions: The object was modelled, shaded, lit and rendered by you in this project.
The integration holds up when paused on any frame of the shot.
You scored all six craft categories honestly from zero to ten.
stretchGoals: Render a second version with one lighting choice reversed and compare the read.
reflectionPrompt: Where did the integration nearly break, and which craft would fix it fastest?

title: The Final Showcase
summary: The closing assessment: one piece that stands as the portfolio opener.
description: This is an assessment, not a lesson. Deliver one complete piece you would put first in a portfolio: story, image, motion, sound and grade all owned by you. Nothing here is new craft — it is every craft at once. Then score all six categories honestly and read the weakest one as your next season.
deliverables: One finished piece of 45 to 120 seconds, exported at delivery quality.
victoryConditions: The piece runs between 45 and 120 seconds and is exported at delivery settings.
Every stage from idea to grade was handled by you inside this project.
You scored all six craft categories honestly from zero to ten.
stretchGoals: Write the one-line pitch you would put under it in a portfolio.
reflectionPrompt: If you had one more week, which single craft category would you spend it all on?
